problem: Embodied-AI capabilities (manipulation VLAs, spatial understanding, navigation, humanoid control) remain specialized modules or loosely coupled loops. They lack an execution interface that composes heterogeneous skills, grounds them in persistent 3D memory, tracks partial progress, and recovers from physical failures.
motivation: LLM agents succeed in digital settings through a reason-act-observe-revise loop, but physical skills are continuous, embodiment-dependent, uncertain, and unsafe to fail, so the loop does not transfer directly (the 'embodiment gap'). The paper treats long-horizon embodied execution as a system-organization problem that needs typed skills, persistent spatial/temporal memory, and runtime monitoring.
key_idea: Wrap heterogeneous robot skill backends (navigation, manipulation, whole-body motion) in a closed-loop Embodied AgentOS that plans skill graphs over a persistent hierarchical 3D spatial and temporal memory and re-plans from typed status feedback over ROS2.
insight: Wrapping a hierarchical-memory navigation backend (FSR-VLN) with the AgentOS loop, which adds candidate verification, feedback-driven state updates and recovery, gives gains in both SR and SPL (simulation: SR 80.8→82.6, SPL 41.0→42.8; real robot: Top-1@1m 91.95→97.70). The gains are modest and there is no ablation isolating individual components, so the evidence supports the loop as a wrapper but not which part matters. On real robots the identical scores across 1/2/3 m thresholds indicate the remaining failures are recovery failures, not localization tolerance.
method: Embodied AgentOS layer: parses voice/text into a skill graph with ordering, preconditions and recovery dependencies; the scheduler dispatches ready skills, consumes status, and triggers clarification or re-planning.

Typed skill interface: each skill declares command, typed parameters, preconditions and expected effects, and publishes progress/success/failure mode/confidence/latency/recoverability over a ROS2 command/status bus; backends are HoloNavi (navigation), HoloBrain (VLA manipulation), HoloMotion (humanoid whole-body).

HoloNavi: an LLM parses the goal, fast CLIP matching over the HMSG retrieves rooms/views/objects, a VLM verifies candidate views (FSR-VLN style fast-to-slow), and frontier/active exploration is triggered when verification fails or the memory is stale.
Geometry memory: a LiDAR-inertial-visual backend (FAST-LIVO) or a vision-only multi-camera backend (GeoFlow-SLAM++ with a 3D foundation model for depth, multi-view optical flow, BoW relocalization).
Semantic memory: SAM2 masks with fused SigLIP descriptors (full frame, masked segment, bounding box, per-dimension weighted); online 3D instance association via projected-mask IoU.

HMSG plus temporal memory: floor/room/view/object scene graph as the retrieval index; temporal memory stores goal/plan state, execution/recovery traces and outcome summaries; incremental subgraph updates from new observations, skill outcomes and user feedback.
Cross-embodiment coordination: robots share one hierarchical 3D memory and typed skill calls; AgentOS binds skills to embodiments by capability, location, availability and safety.

setting.backbone: LLM planner and VLM verifier (unspecified, frozen); CLIP/SigLIP, SAM2, open-vocabulary detector; HoloBrain VLA and HoloMotion controllers as skill backends
setting.training_data: none for the framework itself (composes pretrained models); HoloBrain and HoloMotion are trained separately
setting.observation: RGB-D (multi-camera RGB for the vision-only backend), IMU/LiDAR optional, audio
setting.action_space: typed skill calls (move_to, find, pick, place, etc.) executed by backends; navigation via target poses/frontier routes
setting.simulator: HM3D (ObjectNav protocol of MSGNav); repeatable simulated scenes; real robots
setting.privileged: none stated (real-robot eval uses pre-built HMSG memory of the apartments/digital twins)

results: HoloAgentNav reaches SR 82.6 / SPL 42.8 on HM3D-ObjNav, beating FSR-VLN slow-reasoning (80.8/41.0) and MSGNav (74.1/33.4). On real robots it reaches 97.70 Top-1 and 98.90 Top-5 success versus FSR-VLN 91.95/94.25 (Top-1@1m/Top-5@1m 94.25). The semantic memory is best on ScanNet mIoU (31.58) but is below Omni-Map on Replica (29.93 vs 29.06 mIoU is higher, but f-mIoU 57.00 vs 64.42 is lower).
limitations: No standardized end-to-end benchmark for manipulation, whole-body motion and cross-robot coordination; these are qualitative demonstrations only.
No ablations isolating AgentOS components; navigation gains over FSR-VLN are small, and the real-robot evaluation is on one apartment benchmark.
Memory is weaker on large-area entities (Replica frequency-weighted metrics); LLM/VLM planner details are not specified.
